text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Mother and son killed by guerrillas near Beit El settlement; full closure clamped on Ramallah area.
- Jerusalem police commander leaving post in March.
- Palestinian President Arafat says construction of Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem is a grave violation of peace deals with Israel.
- Russian immigrant accused of spying for Russia.
- Foreign Minister Levy says negotiations with Palestinians could be complicated by Egyptian participation.
- Wave of resignations at Scitex.
MAARIV
- Prime Minister Netanyahu demands Arafat hand over killers of Israeli mother and son.
- Finance Minister Meridor says defence budget will grow next year despite government decision to cut overall spending.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli-Palestinian manhunt for guerrilla squad.
- Netanyahu: We won't agree to the Palestinians giving shelter to murderers.
- Seven children left without a mother after guerrilla attack.
- Egyptian foreign minister to visit Israel next week.
GLOBES
- Head of Monopolies Commission leaving post in February.
- Possible mistake in allocation of points in tender for international telephone service in Israel.
JERUSALEM POST
- Mother, son killed in drive-by attack.
- Israeli army enters Ramallah with Palestinian Authority in search for terrorists.
- Meridor: Attacks threaten peace talks.
- Egyptian President Mubarak: Netanyahu promised negotiating role for Egyptian Foreign Minister Moussa.
- Man indicted as KGB spy.
